canvas-01-1.description: The main map of sheet 1 of the October 1923 Sanborn atlas of Bloomsbury, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north close to the top of the page, covers the eastern half of the village on the Hunterdon County side of the Musconetcong River. Brunswick Avenue, Main Street and Railroad Avenue run across the sheet, crossed by Centre Street at the left edge, East Street and Gardner Street; the land east of Gardner Street (blocks 25, 26 and 27) is left blank. Above Brunswick Avenue the long lots of block 3B run back to a driveway along the river, and across the river, in Warren County, Warren road passes a farm with its barn, wagon house and corn cribs reached by a drive. The blocks between Brunswick Avenue and Railroad Avenue are residential, with frame dwellings of one and two storeys, barns and sheds, and a garage with a repair shop on Main Street at Gardner Street. Industry lies along Railroad Avenue and the Central Railroad of New Jersey: the J. S. Pickel & Sons coal and lumber yard with coal bins under the track, the C. W. Vanatta creamery, the Bloomsbury Canning Co. (closed, in the hands of a receiver) with its wood working factory, and the John H. Meyer Silk Co. mill, with winding and weaving rooms. Joseph Stengel's wagon material factory stands on Railroad Avenue near Centre Street, and the J. T. Smith peach basket factory, not in operation in October 1923, near the river at the end of Brunswick Avenue. A foot bridge crosses the river. Water pipes and hydrants are marked along the streets; Gardner Street south of Main Street is noted as not graded.
notes: Railroad Avenue is today's North Street; Centre Street is today's Center Street.
J. T. Smith peach basket factory marked not in operation October 1923; Bloomsbury Canning Co. closed, in the hands of a receiver.
Printed scale 100 ft to an inch; the fitted scale agrees with sheet 2 (50 ft) to about 2 percent.

Printed sheet 1: title, water and fire notes, key map (500 ft to an inch, not configured), location map, legend, specials index, and two map parts at 100 ft to an inch. Part 1 (main, below the heavy line): Brunswick Av., Main and Railroad Av. between Centre, East and Gardner Streets, with the river, Warren road and block 2 north of it; part 2 (inset, top left): Valley Av., High and Church Streets at the Lehigh Valley R.R. station, half a mile south of town. North up, rotation about 26 degrees.

canvas-01-2.description: The inset at the top left of sheet 1 of the October 1923 Sanborn atlas of Bloomsbury, drawn at 100 feet to an inch and framed by a heavy line, shows the small cluster of buildings around the Lehigh Valley Railroad station about half a mile south of the village centre, as the key map on the same sheet indicates. Valley Avenue runs up the left side and Church Street up the right, joined by High Street near the top; block 29 lies above High Street, block 30 below it, and block 28 west of Valley Avenue. The blocks are mostly open ground. A few frame dwellings stand on High Street and Valley Avenue, with a small printing shop with a one-foot press on High Street. Along the bottom the Lehigh Valley Railroad passes with its freight and passenger station, a railroad water tank, and the storage building of the Bloomsbury Graphite Co., tenants of the railroad's property, together with a shed for agricultural implements. A driveway runs parallel to the track, and An iron bridge with a plank floor is marked at Church Street by the track. Vacant fields lie to the east, and the area north of the inset is noted as vacant as far as the Central Railroad of New Jersey. Water pipes and hydrants are marked on Valley Avenue.
notes: Valley Avenue is today's Lehigh Street.
The Lehigh Valley Railroad here is today's Lehigh Line.
Placed from two street junctions and three parcel block corners; the fitted scale is about 4 percent larger than the main part's.

sheet-2.description: Sheet 2 of the October 1923 Sanborn atlas of Bloomsbury, drawn at 50 feet to an inch, covers the centre of the village between the Musconetcong River at the top and the Central Railroad of New Jersey at the bottom, from Church Street and Willow at the left to Centre Street at the right. Brunswick Avenue, Main Street and Railroad Avenue run across the sheet; west of Church Street the lower street is labelled Railroad Av. (North St.). The Bloomsbury Hotel with its garage for forty cars stands at the head race by the river crossing, and the long lots north of Brunswick Avenue run back to a driveway and the hotel garden on the river. Along Brunswick Avenue are dwellings with a general store, a tin shop selling stoves and tinware, a cobbler, an upholstering shop and a building with furniture storage and a lodge room. The public school, with the fire house in its basement, and a split-tire fire alarm gong stand between Brunswick Avenue and Main Street. Main Street has the borough council room, a doctor's office, and a building holding drugs, a bank and a lodge hall, with the Bloomsbury Coal & Lumber Co. lumber sheds and post office opposite. The Presbyterian Church with its parsonage and cemetery fills the block south of Main Street, and the M.E. Church and another cemetery stand west of Church Street. Along the railroad are the freight station, cattle pen, passenger station, a section house, and the J. S. Pickel & Son coal, lumber and agricultural machinery yard with a Massey-Harris farm machinery shed.
notes: Railroad Avenue east of Church Street is today's North Street; Centre Street is today's Center Street; Willow is today's Willow Avenue.
The junction of Brunswick Avenue, Church Street and Willow is about 5 m from today's node; it was left out of the fit.
Fire house in the basement of the public school.

Printed sheet 2, 50 ft to an inch. Centre of town: Brunswick Av., Main Street and Railroad Av. between Church and Centre Streets, Willow at the top left; Musconetcong River along the top, C.R.R. of N.J. along the bottom. One part.

sheet-3-1.description: The main part of sheet 3 of the October 1923 Sanborn atlas of Bloomsbury, drawn at 50 feet to an inch, covers the western edge of the village on the Hunterdon County side, below and right of a heavy line that sets off the part across the river. Willow runs diagonally across the middle of the part, from Church Street at the upper right towards the reservoir pipe at the left, crossed by West Street, which runs down to Railroad Avenue beside the Central Railroad of New Jersey and its forty-foot embankment. Along the race at the top are the Bloomsbury Graphite Co. Foundry Facing Mill No. 1 with its foundry facing warehouse and office, and a lead grinding mill at the head race; nearby are an agricultural implement and wagon house and an ice cream manufactory on Church Street. Below, the lots along Willow and West Street hold frame dwellings with barns, hen houses and a private shop, and C. Heinrich's wood toy manufactory stands near Railroad Avenue. An orchard fills block 6, and vacant fields lie beyond the embankment. A stone arch bridge carries a road over the railroad at the left, and a six-inch water pipe from the reservoir enters along Willow. The river and tail race appear at the top right with the Church Street iron bridge.
notes: Willow is today's Willow Avenue; Railroad Avenue here is today's North Street, whose modern centreline lies north of the drawn one at West Street.
Placed by a hand-picked junction (West Street / Willow) and four parcel block corners on West Street; all lie along one street, so the placement is a similarity transform.
The part above the heavy line (across the river) is drawn displaced and was not placed.

Printed sheet 3, 50 ft to an inch. Part 1 (below and right of the heavy line): Willow, West and Church Streets, Railroad Av. and the C.R.R. of N.J. embankment, Bloomsbury Graphite Co. Foundry Facing Mill No. 1 and the lead grinding mill on the race. Part 2 (above and left of the heavy line, across the river in Warren County): Warren County Road, Bloomsbury Graphite Co. Foundry Facing Mill No. 2, John Lewdrop's blacksmith shop and a farm; drawn displaced, about 140 m south of its true position judging by Warren Glen Road; not placed.

Not georeferenced on this sheet: inset across the river in Warren County: Warren County Road (now Warren Glen Road), Bloomsbury Graphite Co. Foundry Facing Mill No. 2, John Lewdrop blacksmith, farm (drawn displaced from its true position (heavy line); no surviving street junction (the road to the old iron bridge is gone); needs step 6b: hand-picked control, e.g. parcel corners along Warren Glen Road, checked against an aerial).
